problem: Model-free RL mobile manipulation (MM) is sample-inefficient because long trajectories are dominated by redundant navigation data that swamps sparse critical interaction moments. Policies trained on one task also generalize poorly to new spatial layouts, and they forget skills.
motivation: MM is a long-horizon chain of heterogeneous skills with strict sequential dependencies. Early navigation failures block downstream experience, and the buffer fills with navigation fragments. Inspired by neuroscience (recalling episodic fragments and composing them with habitual skills), the paper selects key fragments to train a world model, then uses that model for planning.
key_idea: Train a Dreamer-style RSSM on adaptively prioritized critical experience fragments (LOF outliers, IK failures, prediction error), then use it for CEM-based model-predictive forward planning around a SAC actor-critic, in both training and evaluation, to improve MM skills and transfer them to new layouts without retraining.
insight: Prioritizing rare, critical transitions matters most: removing all AES drops cross-room TCR from 81 to 10, and removing the LOF-based informative selection hurts more (TCR 34) than removing task criticality (TCR 51). MPFP helps in both training (TCR 31 without) and evaluation (68 without). For transfer, removing MPFP lowers TCR in home-scene from 61 to 46, so the imagination-based planner supplies the generalization rather than the policy alone.
method: EE-centric MM formulation: the Husky+UR5 base learns SE(2) continuous 2D actions so the end-effector reaches sequential SE(3) goals. An IK solver handles the arm, and episodes terminate on collision or IK failure. Observations are a 30x30 local occupancy map plus a state vector.
RSSM dynamic model: a Dreamer V3-style latent model with an encoder, recurrent dynamics (h, z), and observation and reward predictors. It is trained concurrently with SAC on a shared replay buffer.

Adaptive Experience Selection (AES): sliding fixed-length windows with the highest total priority are sampled from a SumTree. Priority = w1*max(0, LOF-1) + w2*IK-failure indicator + w3*RSSM prediction loss. All weights are 1.0.

Informative experience selection: Local Outlier Factor over observations, with an L1 distance on the map plus a cosine distance on the state vector, flags rare moments such as door opening, grasping and near-collisions.

Model-Predictive Forward Planning (MPFP): CEM is initialized from the SAC actor. L=50 candidate action sequences of horizon H=8 are unrolled in the RSSM with actor rollouts and predicted rewards. The SAC critic Q gives a terminal value, the top-10 elites refit the Gaussian, and only the first action is executed. H is scheduled from 1 to 8 during training.
Spatial generalization protocol: train once on cross-room MM (navigate, pick, open door, place), then evaluate zero-shot on home-scene, warehouse and dynamic-scene layouts with MPFP planning.

setting.backbone: SAC actor-critic + RSSM (Dreamer V3-style) with 3-layer CNN map encoder and MLP, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: Online RL interaction in simulation, 5x10^6 environment steps per configuration; no external data
setting.observation: Ground-truth robot-centric local occupancy map (30x30, 0.1 m) + proprioceptive state vector (previous action, joint states, EE pose/velocity, goal EE pose)
setting.action_space: Continuous 2D mobile-base velocity/placement commands; arm motion via IK solver
setting.simulator: N2M2-style ROS/PyBullet MM simulation (cross-room, warehouse, home-scene, dynamic-scene)
setting.privileged: Ground-truth local occupancy maps (stated limitation); goal EE poses given

numbers.extra: trained and evaluated in the same configuration; 5M steps
trained on cross-room only, no additional training

numbers_note: Custom MM benchmarks (N2M2 configurations), not navigation benchmarks. TCR and PSR are percentages. Ablation rows (Table 4, Table 3 w/o MPFP) are omitted, except as cited in insight.
results: In the cross-room setting the method reaches TCR 81 / PSR 54, versus the strongest baseline AuxDistill (TCR 57 / PSR 42) and Dreamer V3 (54 / 40). It also cuts AIKF from 8.1-11.3 to 4.1. Zero-shot transfer to home-scene reaches TCR 61 versus 44 for Dreamer V3 and 29 for N2M2. ABC is sometimes worse, as in dynamic scenes, which the authors attribute to longer episodes.
limitations: Uses ground-truth local occupancy maps, so the idealized perception assumption is untested with noisy sensor-built maps.
Collision counts are sometimes worse than baselines, especially in dynamic scenes; real-world evidence is limited and detailed in the supplement.
MPFP planning adds test-time compute (50 candidates x horizon 8 with CEM iterations per step), and the generalization is tested only on simulated layouts with a single robot.
